note: Accounts worth studying for MECHANICS. Maintained by hand; the research agent reads this list and never adds to it on its own, because who is worth watching is a judgement.
hardLine: We record what a post DOES. We never record how it is written. Voice belongs to the account that built it and copying it produces an impression of a person rather than a post of our own.
accessNote: Reading these timelines through the API is TECHNICALLY AVAILABLE to our credentials (verified 2026-08-26, HTTP 200, 900 req/15min) and priced per post read. See research/x-api-access.md for what that costs and why the archive is fed by hand and by the daily web pass rather than by polling.

accounts.watchFor: Long-form lore and illustrator posts, and the two formats an earlier review of this account MISSED: the outside reference and the narrative pair. Both were his strongest and both were invisible to a review that was looking for what it could automate.
accounts.sourced: data/knowledge.json — an Atsuko Nishida appreciation at 15.7K views, a Miki Kudo one at 15.4K; runs numbered daily series as a signature format

accounts.watchFor: The PERMISSION mechanic — a second sentence that removes the reason not to answer. This is the best-documented reply engine we have observed.
accounts.sourced: data/knowledge.json — roughly 900 replies on one post at ~16k followers

accounts.watchFor: The same permission mechanic in a different register, and an unusually high reply-to-like ratio: 68 replies against 73 likes on 'Not my opinion, I want to know what people really think'. Replies outnumbering likes is the signal worth understanding.
accounts.sizeNote: ~17.6k followers; a 37,100-view post is on record

accounts.watchFor: SET_DOUBT. 'Is Team Up actually a good set or does it just have the lovebirds?' — 17 replies on 15,000 views, 1.13 per thousand against our own best of 0.27.
accounts.sourced: Tyler-supplied observation 2026-08-25, ratio recomputed from data/post-outcomes.json

accounts.watchFor: ERA_CLAIM. A short arguable claim about an era over cropped art, inviting a counter-era.
A small account worth watching precisely BECAUSE it is small — the mechanics that work at 3k are the ones that work without reach behind them.
accounts.sourced: data/knowledge.json — the accounts worth studying are mostly small

accounts.watchFor: The only large account on this list. Included as a CONTRAST: what works at 364k may work because of reach rather than because of the mechanic, and telling those apart is the point of watching it.
